setting: Municipal pool locker room after swim practice
topic: Creating inclusion for a transgender teammate
summary: Kelda asks Theron how to support a trans teammate facing locker-room whispers.
plan: Kelda plans to organize a group of teammates to publicly announce their support for the trans teammate during the next team meeting, believing that a visible show of solidarity in front of everyone will silence the locker-room whispers.
flaw: A public group declaration in front of the whole team can backfire by making the trans teammate the center of unwanted attention, and it doesn't address the private gossipers, who are unlikely to change their behavior just because of a staged show of support.

setting: city procurement review room with bid binders
topic: evaluating low-bid proposals for parking garage repairs
summary: Stellan asks Marwa how to evaluate a low-bid proposal for parking garage repairs.
plan: Stellan plans to evaluate the parking garage repair bids by ranking each contractor's proposal solely on the lowest quoted price per repair line item, assuming that adding up the cheapest line items will identify the best overall low bid.
flaw: Comparing bids line by line at the lowest price assumes all contractors listed identical scopes, but bids often group work differently or exclude items another bid includes, so the cheapest sum may not be an apples-to-apples comparison and may not even reflect the true lowest compliant bid.

setting: living room video setup with yarn baskets
topic: demonstrating knitting techniques for left-handed learners
summary: Jules asks Ioana for advice on filming a knitting tutorial for left-handed viewers.
plan: Jules plans to film the tutorial in a mirror so that left-handed viewers can simply copy the mirrored motions directly, treating the reflection as a straightforward way to flip the demonstration.
flaw: Mirroring the footage reverses the image but does not change the actual stitch mechanics; a left-handed knitter following a mirrored right-handed demo still ends up with the working yarn and needle positions on the wrong side, so the motions won't produce the intended result without re-teaching the hand positioning.

summary: Adelina asks Yori for help arranging origami butterflies across a hospital room wall.
plan: Adelina plans to attach the origami butterflies directly to the wall with rolled loops of masking tape, reasoning that tape is gentle enough for hospital surfaces and easy to remove later.
flaw: Masking tape's adhesive dries out and loses tack quickly on painted walls, especially in a warm ward, so the butterflies will start peeling off within a day or two and need constant re-taping.

setting: soup kitchen pantry stacked with donated cans
topic: turning donated ingredients into balanced community meals
summary: Ulani asks Fintan in a soup kitchen pantry how to stretch donated ingredients into balanced meals.
plan: Ulani plans to stretch the donated canned goods by blending several different cans of soup together into one large pot, assuming that mixing them will average out each can's shortcomings and produce a more balanced meal.
flaw: Combining soups only dilutes flavors and nutrients proportionally; it doesn't add missing food groups, so if the donated soups are all low in protein or vegetables, the blended result remains just as unbalanced.

setting: shared photography studio beside charging stations
topic: choosing a backup strategy for high-volume photo archives
summary: Gwen asks Ryo for help selecting a backup strategy for a photographer collective.
plan: Gwen plans to keep one copy of the collective's high-volume raw archive on a single large external hard drive that stays plugged into the studio workstation, treating that drive as the backup since it is separate from the computer's internal disk.
flaw: A drive that stays connected to the same workstation is not a real backup: it is vulnerable to the same theft, power surge, ransomware, or accidental deletion as the primary copy, so it offers no protection against the most common loss scenarios.

setting: cider mill processing room during harvest
topic: testing pasteurization temperature probes in cider production
summary: Hanneli asks Ciro how to test pasteurization temperature probes on a cider line.
plan: Hanneli plans to verify each pasteurization probe by immersing it in a pot of boiling water and treating 212°F as the reference point, assuming any probe reading close to that at the boil is accurate across the pasteurization range.
flaw: Boiling water only checks one point at the top of the scale, and the reading there will shift with local atmospheric pressure and elevation, so it doesn't confirm accuracy at the actual pasteurization temperatures. A single-point check at the boil can't detect errors in the mid-range where the probes actually operate.

topic: verifying allergen cleaning between production runs
summary: Belen asks Kareem how to verify allergen cleaning after switching granola flavors.
plan: Belen plans to verify that the allergen cleaning between granola flavor runs was successful by visually inspecting the mixers and conveyors for any leftover crumbs or residue, assuming that if the equipment looks spotless, no cross-contact allergens remain.
flaw: The flaw is that allergen residues, like trace almond or peanut proteins, can remain on equipment even when no visible particles are present, since a visually clean surface is not the same as a chemically clean one. Verification needs a test such as an allergen-specific protein swab rather than a visual check.

topic: writing a hazard analysis for kombucha bottling
summary: Phoebe asks Hassan how to prepare a hazard analysis for a kombucha bottling line.
plan: Phoebe believes that a hazard analysis for kombucha bottling only needs to cover biological hazards, like pathogen growth from the live cultures, since fermentation is the main risk area.
flaw: A proper hazard analysis must also consider chemical and physical hazards, such as glass shards from broken bottles, cleaning chemical residues, and acidity-related leaching from packaging materials. Limiting the analysis to biological hazards alone would leave the bottling line's other risk categories unaddressed.

setting: Observatory lawn under a portable telescope
topic: Choosing between family expectations and personal calling
summary: Aya asks Lionel whether to study astronomy or follow her parents' plan for law school.
plan: Aya plans to resolve her dilemma by proving to her parents that astronomy is the practical choice, since she believes astrophysics graduates earn higher average starting salaries than law graduates.
flaw: The salary comparison is backwards: law graduates, especially those entering corporate practice, typically have higher average starting salaries than recent astrophysics graduates, whose early academic and research positions pay modestly. So the evidence she plans to present would likely backfire and undermine her argument.
